SYNTHETIC reversal.error: this series is not monotone, so a four-parameter logistic is the wrong model for it and no EC50 fitted to it would mean anything. The response turns around at 1 uM: the reversal against the trend is 100% of the response span (Spearman rho -0.03, 1 sign change(s)). A bell shape in a concentration series is almost always cytotoxicity at the top dose killing the signal that was being measured. Re-fit without the top dose, or use a biphasic model — spaCR does not have one. Set allow_non_monotone=True to force a fit, and expect the EC50 to be an artefact of where the curve turns.

07_inhibition_midpoint.report:
4PL dose–response · SYNTHETIC inhibition (27 observations, 9 concentrations from 0.01 uM to 100 uM).

  EC50 = 1.5 uM (95% profile CI 1.47 uM – 1.53 uM, a factor of 1 either way); Hill slope -1.20 (inhibition); plateaus 5 to 95; 27 observations at 9 concentrations.

  residual SE 0.4423 on 23 df; R² 0.9999
  lack of fit vs pure error: F = 0 on 5, 18 df, p = 1 — consistent with a 4PL

  ! R² is 0.9999, and it is nearly useless here: almost any monotone curve through a dose–response scores above 0.95, because the total sum of squares is dominated by the gap between the plateaus. Read the residual standard error (0.4423, in response units) and the lack-of-fit test instead.
  ! 3 vehicle observation(s) at concentration 0 were excluded from the fit (log10(0) has no value) and averaged 95. Compare that with the fitted low-dose plateau: they should agree, and a gap means the series never got back to control.

downloadable_example.byte_difference: Download uses LF, capture input CRLF; all 120 parsed CSV records are identical.

oracle_scope: Closed-form planted curves, raw observations, independent SVD/profile roots, analytic-Jacobian Wald intervals and actual plotted artists; no app fitting helper used as its own expected answer.
profile_precision: Implementation declares 0.001-wide log10 root brackets. Midpoint endpoint checks allow half that width, not an SSE tolerance or statistical coverage guarantee.
